chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abi Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The people say that the Throne (al-Arsh) shook at the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.' He said: 'It was only the bed (al-sarir) upon which he was lying.'

key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ مُعَاذٍ: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, a prominent companion

ai.seo_question: Did the Throne of God shake when Sa'd ibn Mu'adh died?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects a popular exaggeration regarding the cosmic reaction to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's death, specifying that the shaking occurred to his bed (*sarir*) rather than the Divine Throne (*Arsh*). This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise attribution of miraculous events (*karamat*) to avoid conflating human honor with divine attributes, while affirming the high status of the companion. The clarification serves to ground spiritual narratives in historical reality, ensuring that reverence for the righteous does not lead to theological ambiguity regarding the majesty of Allah.
